title: Helvetic Republic
capsule: The Helvetic Republic (Helvetische Republik) was a French sister republic proclaimed on 12 April 1798 following the invasion of the Swiss Confederation by French Revolutionary forces under General Brune, which abolished the cantonal sovereignty that had defined Swiss politics since 1291. Modeled on the French Directory, it established a centralized unitary state with a bicameral legislature and freedom of the press, abolishing serfdom and internal tariffs. Persistent federal resistance — most violently in the Nidwalden and Obwalden uprising (September 1798) — and chronic financial crisis rendered it ungovernable; Napoleon Bonaparte imposed the Act of Mediation in February 1803, restoring cantonal sovereignty. The Helvetic period nonetheless left permanent legal legacies including property registration and civil equality; the dataset's end-date of 1815 reflects the Congress of Vienna settlement that confirmed Swiss perpetual neutrality.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic was coterminous with the former Swiss Confederation boundaries, which are well established; its brief existence is fully documented, but the 1815 end-date in the dataset encompasses the Restoration period beyond the republic's 1803 dissolution.
